instruction.text: Estimate the answer to the problem. First make a suitable estimation sum, then solve it.

atoms.a:
On Saturday at Manchester Airport, 176726 passengers were counted, and on Sunday there were 191764.

Round each number to the nearest thousand. How many passengers, to the nearest thousand, were at Manchester Airport at the weekend?
atoms.b:
Estimation sum: 177000 192000 + 177000 192000 = 369000

Answer: Around 369000 people flew either from or to Manchester.

atoms.a:
A charity is collecting donations for one of their projects. At a charity gala £306,714 was collected. At a charitable auction a further £97,497 was raised.

Round each number to the nearest ten thousand. How much money, to the nearest ten thousand, was the charity able to raise?
atoms.b:
Estimation sum: £310000 100000+ £100000 310000 = £410000

Answer: They were able to raise around £410000.

atoms.a:
A total of 13350 litres of drinks were bought for a festival. Over the course of the weekend, 11478 litres were drunk.

Round each number to the nearest hundred. How many litres of drinks, to the nearest hundred, were left over?
atoms.b:
Estimation sum: 13400l - 11500l = 1900l

Answer: There were around 1900 litres of drinks left over.

atoms.a:
At the FA Cup final, 76197 spectators watched the game in the stadium. 44961 spectators were fans of Chelsea or were neutrals.

Round each number to the nearest thousand. How many fans of Liverpool, to the nearest thousand, were in the stadium?
atoms.b:
Estimation sum: 76000 - 45000 = 31000

Answer: There were around 31000 Liverpool fans in the stadium.
